newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market active at $71 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market active at $71 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Thursday were active at $71.00 per cwt, down $2.00 from top prices last week, feedlot sources said.

About 20,000-25,000 head were sold from Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma feedlots and 25,500 from Kansas, the sources said. Prices weakened late Wednesday and Thursday as beef prices wilted, market sources said.

Midday beef was quoted down $0.27 to $0.85 per cwt, with 170 fabricated loads sold, according to USDA. Choice heavyweight cuts have fallen $1.27 this week, despite a decline in slaughter, indicating weaker demand, they said.
Thursday's slaughter was estimated 131,000 head, which brought the week-to-date number to 476,000, USDA said. The weekly figure was down 1.0 percent from a week ago and 6.8 percent from a year ago.
Weak feedlot cattle prices were expected to be offset early next week if carryover from this week's showlist is light and numbers of market-ready cattle are tight, the market sources said.
Some feedlots reported packers had bought cattle with a few extra days allowed for delivery so they would be assured inventory in the event supplies were tight next week.
